clue.text: Fill up-seconds consumed

parts.note: consumed means ate, as of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone tops up their plate, the second helpings already eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy an appetite completely, which is to fill someone up.

clue.text: After school, avoid looking up timetable

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the word for school
in a down clue looking up means the word for avoid is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to avoid is to elude

explanation.surface: Once classes are over, someone avoids checking the timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a plan listing times of events, a programme.

clue.text: Specifically stated old money allowed

parts.note: ex means former, old
P stands for pence, money
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Clear terms were laid down for permitted pre-decimal coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Girl's performance may cause unease

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with the possessive 's kept
a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: A young woman's stage show might leave the audience uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to unsettle them, making them uneasy.

clue.text: Bore, only catching female insect

parts.note: a drag is a bore, something tedious

indicators.note: catching shows one word holding another letter inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tedious person who only catches a woman's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts F inside ONLY to make ONFLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a long-bodied winged creature, a type of flying bug.

clue.text: Give and take in economic law?

parts.note: to supply is to give
taken as written
to demand is to take or claim

explanation.surface: Asks about the give and take of an economic principle.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle that prices settle where availability meets buyers' wants is a core rule of economics.

clue.text: Showing agreement, though hardly paying attention

definitions.meaning: moving the head down and up to say yes

explanation.definitionFit: Bowing the head in assent and dozing off in a chair share this word.

clue.text: Fussy eaters may give us recipe

indicators.note: may give suggests the letters can produce something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Picky diners might hand over their cooking instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicures are people with refined taste in food, discerning gourmets.

clue.text: The corps is in attendance

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A military unit has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To be there is to be present at a place, attending.

clue.text: Housework the French see as a fair challenge

parts.note: the word splits as house, abbreviated HO, and work, abbreviated OP for opus
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: French people regard the household chores as a test laid on at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housework' must be split into house (HO) and work (OP, from opus) before it gives anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoop-la is a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes, a challenge at a fair.

clue.text: Mere existence?

parts.note: a mere is a small lake, a pond
existence means life

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is merely living and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is the noun for a lake; the life of a mere is creatures living in ponds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pond-life is the creatures living in still water, the existence found in a lake.

clue.text: Mask game piece that would be spotted

definitions.meaning: a small eye mask worn at masquerades

definitions.text: game piece that would be spotted
definitions.meaning: a ... tile is marked with spots or pips

explanation.definitionFit: Both a carnival half-mask and a pip-marked gaming tile share this name.

clue.text: Allowance for being busy in frantic duel

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other
frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters of duel are jumbled

parts.note: being busy is being at it

explanation.surface: Leeway is granted to people caught up in a wild fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' alone suggests a single synonym, but the phrase 'being busy' gives 'at it'; 'frantic' scrambles the duel letters and 'in' places the busy phrase among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action, the scope or leeway someone is allowed.

clue.text: It may be daring, if demeaning

indicators.note: it may be suggests the letters can become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold act can also be humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may be' rearranges DARING and IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means beneath one's dignity, undignified.

clue.text: Cromwell's cavalry press on the flanks

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
the flanks are the sides

explanation.surface: Cromwell's horsemen push forward on both wings.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell's troopers in the English Civil War earned the nickname of their commander.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parliamentarian horse soldiers of the 1640s were known by this name, after Cromwell himself.

clue.text: One playing bridge in beastly surroundings

indicators.note: the word beastly is the surroundings that enclose the answer

explanation.surface: A card player sits in a nasty, savage setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, one of them seated at this position.

clue.text: Bob turns out obstinate

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bob proves to be pig-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' rearranges BOB and TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means refusing to change one's mind, headstrong.

clue.text: Way back, a king-emperor

indicators.note: back means the letters for way are read in the other direction

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Long ago there lived a ruler who was both king and emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor bore this title, from Latin Caesar.

clue.text: Instruct set is to be arranged in packing-case

parts.note: to instruct is to teach

indicators.note: is to be arranged tells us the letters of set are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An order to sort out a set of things into a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to be arranged' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box once used to ship tea, now a household storage crate.

clue.text: Very prompt with cash on top of table

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: readies is British slang for ready cash

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word table

explanation.surface: Money is laid out on top of the table, ready and waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: READIES is British slang for banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiest is the superlative of ready, meaning the quickest to act.

clue.text: Characteristic pattern-men dry, so get drunk

indicators.note: getting drunk throws things into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Teetotal men, so they say, end up drinking: a familiar pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get drunk' rearranges MEN, DRY and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a recognisable set of symptoms or behaviours occurring together.

clue.text: Last three in bookmakers arranged to take evidence of debts to grave

indicators.note: arranged means those chosen letters are placed in a new order
last three in picks the final three letters of the word bookmakers

parts.note: IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Bookies' records of what is owed follow someone to the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last three in' takes ERS from bookmakers and 'arranged' turns it into SER.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious both mean solemn and weighty.

clue.text: Make free with money-I chide

parts.note: L stands for pound, from libra, a unit of money
to chide is to berate or scold

explanation.surface: Someone takes liberties with cash while scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set at liberty, releasing from captivity.

clue.text: Part of coat some call a pelisse

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fur-trimmed cloak is what some would call a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded front flap of a jacket below the collar.

clue.text: Back for a place

definitions.meaning: to back a motion is to ... it, support it

explanation.definitionFit: Supporting a proposal and the runner-up position in a race share this word.

clue.text: Professional to create a type of invoice

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to form is to create or make

explanation.surface: A specialist is hired to design a billing document.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a preliminary bill sent before goods are supplied.

clue.text: Excavator driver goes to the boundary

parts.note: DR is a short form used for driver
the boundary is the edge

explanation.surface: A motorist heads off to the very limit of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredge is a machine that scoops mud from riverbeds, a digging device.

clue.text: Natural disasters led islands to destruction

indicators.note: destruction breaks things apart, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Catastrophes brought a group of islands to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Landslides are collapses of earth and rock down slopes, a kind of natural catastrophe.

clue.text: Solicitor takes time out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout is someone who pesters people for business, one who solicits.
